cf.title: DirtySnapshot index scan skips concurrently updated tuples leading to lost updates/deletes in logical replication

verdict_reasoning: The problem is stated and reproduced by two other people, so levels 1a and 1b pass. Two fixable level 2 objections survive, replication-ondisk-1 and standards-compat-1, both about the in-flight local INSERT case measured in message #44. A committer who knows the apply worker must decide whether that behaviour change is acceptable, in particular on stable branches. The v20 patch and its discussion are in a thread not shown here, so confidence is low.

brief.title: Fix missed tuples in SnapshotDirty index scans used by logical replication apply
brief.problem: A btree index scan with SnapshotDirty or SnapshotSelf can return no row when a concurrent non-HOT update of that row puts the new index entry on the same page, or on a page to the left. RelationFindReplTupleByIndex uses such a scan, so the subscriber apply worker can lose publisher updates or deletes and report the wrong conflict type.
brief.proposed_design: The current version (v11 to v20) scans with a fresh MVCC snapshot from GetLatestSnapshot before each attempt in the logical replication tuple lookup, and table_tuple_lock still waits for concurrent updaters. Earlier versions tracked max(xmax) and rescanned (v1 to v4, dropped by the author as unsound), then held btree page read locks longer (v5 to v10). A test patch adds injection points and TAP tests.
user_visible_surface: Logical replication conflict reports (update_missing, delete_missing, update_origin_differs, update_deleted) change for concurrent subscriber updates.
An in-flight local INSERT of the same key is no longer waited for, so the apply worker reports update_missing and skips the publisher UPDATE.
New injection points for tests, now in heapam_index_getnext_slot().
author_claims: The race exists in every release since logical replication and since the first UPSERT commit.
Concurrent subscriber updates, even to subscriber-only columns, can make publisher updates or deletes get lost.
The MVCC scan gives the same guarantees as SnapshotDirty, without missed tuples and with the same performance.
Master only wins the in-flight INSERT race by chance, so v20 leaves the wait out.
brief.thread_state: Amit Kapila questioned whether SnapshotDirty results are wrong and suggested documenting the race; Manu rebased to v19, confirmed the tests fail without the fix, and showed an in-flight INSERT regression with a variant that keeps the wait. The author declined the variant and moved v20 to a separate thread, not shown here.
unclear: The v20 patch and its discussion are in another thread and not visible here.
The material does not show whether a committer agrees this is a bug to back-patch to stable branches.
No benchmark exists for the MVCC rescan or for Manu's extra SnapshotDirty pass.
The material does not say whether check_exclusion_or_unique_constraint and other SnapshotDirty callers stay unfixed.
The documentation patch for the logical replication race lives in a third thread and its state is not shown.
search_queries: nbtree page lock dirty snapshot race

objections.title: MVCC lookup drops the wait for an in-flight local INSERT
objections.failure_scenario: A subscriber session has an uncommitted INSERT of key 1 when the publisher's UPDATE of key 1 arrives. Under v19/v20 the apply worker does not wait, so it logs update_missing and skips the UPDATE. The subscriber keeps 'fromsub' while the publisher has 'frompubnew', and the user only learns this from the conflict log or from diverged data.
objections.argument: Message #44 measured this five times: master waits, applies the UPDATE and reports no conflict, while the patch loses the UPDATE. In message #45 the author says master only wins this race by chance, so v20 leaves the wait out. A committer would likely see a lost update moved from one case to another, because the conflict-detection code relies on the wait. Manu's variant keeps the wait and does not bring the concurrent-update race back, and the material gives no reason why it is unsound.
objections.author_must_show: Which case does the extra SnapshotDirty pass from message #44 handle incorrectly, and why is losing the in-flight INSERT wait better than keeping it?

critic.reasoning: Message #36 argues only the INSERT versus INSERT case, and message #45 points to another thread for the reasons. The visible material does not say which case the extra SnapshotDirty pass from message #44 handles wrongly.

objections.title: Back-patched fix changes the in-flight local INSERT outcome from apply to skip
objections.failure_scenario: A subscriber application has a local INSERT of key 1 still open when the publisher's UPDATE of key 1 arrives. Today the apply worker waits, then applies the UPDATE. After a minor upgrade it reports update_missing, skips the UPDATE and keeps the local row, and the divergence shows up only when someone compares the two nodes.
objections.argument: Message #44 measured this case in 5 runs on each tree: master waited and applied the UPDATE every time, and v19 skipped it every time. The author answers in message #45 that master only wins a race here, but the measured master behaviour is a lock wait followed by a decision, and that is repeatable. The CF entry targets stable, so users would get this change in a minor release without asking for it. Manu's variant keeps the wait, and the material does not show why it was declined.
objections.author_must_show: Why should a stable-branch fix change the outcome for an in-flight local INSERT, when the variant in message #44 keeps master's behaviour and passes the same tests?

critic.reasoning: Message #44 measured the change on both trees, and the CommitFest entry targets stable. The author's reason for declining the variant that keeps the wait is in a thread not shown here, so nothing visible answers the minor-release question.

refuted.title: Back-patch changes subscriber conflict behaviour in minor releases
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator applies a minor update to a subscriber on a stable branch. Concurrent local writes then produce different conflict types (update_missing where master waited and applied before), and fewer missed rows. Monitoring or resolution scripts keyed on those types start acting differently with no release note.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry targets stable, and the brief lists changed conflict reports as user-visible. Message #44 shows that one of these changes skips a publisher UPDATE that current releases apply. No committer in the material has agreed this is a back-patchable bug, and Amit Kapila suggested documenting the race instead (message #34). The test patch hooks heapam_index_getnext_slot(), which exists only on master after the rebase in message #44.
refuted.author_must_show: Which stable branches should get the fix, and how would the in-flight INSERT behaviour change be justified in a minor release?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The other parts do not add a failure: corrected conflict types are the purpose of the fix, and where the test injection point lives is an implementation detail outside levels 1-2.

refuted.title: Fix covers one caller and leaves the SnapshotDirty btree limitation for the others
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch, such as a conflict resolver or an extension, runs a SnapshotDirty or SnapshotSelf index scan and assumes a committed row is always found. Under a concurrent non-HOT update it gets no row and acts on that wrong answer. Nothing fails loudly, and the bug shows up only as rare field reports.
refuted.argument: Message #4 and message #31 state that every SnapshotDirty or SnapshotSelf btree scan can miss a live tuple. Since v11 the fix changes only RelationFindReplTupleByIndex. check_exclusion_or_unique_constraint keeps the behaviour and relies on retry logic, and the brief lists that caller as not fixed. A README note documents the race, but no assertion or API rule stops a new caller from depending on a complete result.
refuted.author_must_show: What stops a future SnapshotDirty or SnapshotSelf index scan caller from assuming complete results, beyond the README note?

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on a future caller that does not exist, and the limitation predates this patch. Messages #4, #13 and #14 explain why the existing callers in check_exclusion_or_unique_constraint are safe through retry and speculative insertion.

refuted.title: Target 'stable' brings a conflict-behaviour change into back branches
refuted.failure_scenario: A subscriber on a stable branch has a local INSERT of a key still open when a publisher UPDATE of that key arrives. Before a minor release the apply worker waits and applies the UPDATE. After it, the worker reports update_missing and drops the UPDATE, and the user learns this from changed data or conflict counts after the upgrade.
refuted.argument: Message #44 measured this change and offered a variant that keeps the wait. Message #45 declined it on the grounds that master only wins that race by chance. That argument may support changing master, but a minor release that turns one lost-update case into another is hard to defend. The tests also hook into heapam_index_getnext_slot(), which does not exist on older branches, so each back branch needs its own injection points.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the fix meant for back branches, and if so, why is dropping the in-flight INSERT wait acceptable in a minor release?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which states the same in-flight INSERT change in a minor release with the same evidence. The per-branch injection point remark concerns test code, which is outside levels 1-2.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The fix changes how the logical replication apply worker finds the subscriber row in RelationFindReplTupleByIndex.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets stable, and the fix changes conflict outcomes that users of current releases can observe.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The apply worker lookup gets a new snapshot rule, and new injection points sit in heapam_index_getnext_slot().

touch_points.reason: The apply worker takes a fresh snapshot with GetLatestSnapshot before each lookup attempt, and no benchmark is shown.

questions: Which case does the extra SnapshotDirty pass from message #44 handle incorrectly?
Why is skipping the publisher UPDATE with update_missing better than waiting for the in-flight local INSERT, as master does in the five runs of message #44?
Which stable branches should get the fix, and how is the in-flight INSERT behaviour change justified in a minor release?
What does the fresh MVCC snapshot per lookup attempt cost the apply worker on an update-heavy workload, compared with master?
Does the fix leave check_exclusion_or_unique_constraint and other SnapshotDirty callers as they are, and is that intended?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the logical replication apply worker and conflict detection, with a second opinion from someone who knows nbtree scans with non-MVCC snapshots. The brief shows Amit Kapila questioning the premise and suggesting documentation; no committer in the visible material has agreed to the fix.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the conflict detection results of the apply worker on every branch that gets the fix, including the changed in-flight INSERT outcome. On stable branches this holds until each branch reaches end of life.
committability.author_follow_up: Strong sign that the author stays: more than two years of work, 20 versions, and repeated moves between CommitFests by the author.

priority.reason: The fix prevents lost publisher updates and deletes on subscribers that also take local writes, and the current design is confined to the tuple lookup of the apply worker. The entry has been in 11 CommitFests, and no committer in the visible material has ruled on the in-flight INSERT trade-off or on back-patching.

provisional_note: The v20 patch, its thread and the related documentation thread are not shown, and no code was read. The author's reasons for declining the variant in message #44 could not be checked, nor could the cost of the extra snapshot.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
Reverted commit(s): VACUUM: ignore indexing operations with CONCURRENTLY
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit d9d076222f5b "VACUUM: ignore indexing operations
with CONCURRENTLY".

These changes caused indexes created with the CONCURRENTLY option to
miss heap tuples that were HOT-updated and HOT-pruned during the index
creation.  Before these changes, HOT pruning would have been prevented
by the Xmin of the transaction creating the index, but because this
change was precisely to allow the Xmin to move forward ignoring that
backend, now other backends scanning the table can prune them.  This is
not a problem for VACUUM (which requires a lock that conflicts with a
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY operation), but HOT-prune can definitely
occur.  In other words, Xmin advancement was sped up, but at the cost of
corrupting the resulting index.

Regrettably, this means that the new feature in PG14 that RIC/CIC on
very large tables no longer force VACUUM to retain very old tuples goes
away.  We might try to implement it again in a later release, but for
now the risk of indexes missing tuples is too high and there's no easy
fix.

Backpatch to 14, where this change appeared.

Diagnosys-by: Andrey Borodin <x4mmm@yandex-team.ru>
Diagnosys-by: Michael Paquier <michael@paquier.xyz>
Diagnosys-by: Andres Freund <andres@anarazel.de>

precedents_retrieved.title: Global snapshots
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add Clock-SI based global snapshots to core: a new SLRU mapping xids to a physical-clock-based GlobalCSN, an InDoubt commit state, snapshot import/export and global prepare/assign SQL functions, and delayed oldestXmin advancement so snapshots can be shared across Postgres instances. postgres_fdw would use this infrastructure with a minimal 2PC to give cross-node transactions snapshot isolation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was rebased in November 2018, but the further work the author planned (including a line-by-line review by committers) did not happen before the commitfest closed. Andres Freund proposed marking it returned with feedback, and the author agreed, saying it would not realistically go in during the last commitfest and would be reopened in the next release cycle. Robert Haas had asked for further research on the design, but the visible messages show the entry was closed for lack of progress, not because of a decisive technical objection.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This hasn't happened yet, so I think this ought to be marked ad returned
with feedback?

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
Reverted commit(s): Fix index-only scan plans when not all index columns can be returned.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 4ace45677 failed to fix the problem fully, because the
same issue of attempting to fetch a non-returnable index column
can occur when rechecking the indexqual after using a lossy index
operator.  Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which
indicates a gap in our test cases :-().

Revert the code changes of 4ace45677 in favor of adding a new field
to struct IndexOnlyScan, containing a version of the indexqual that
can be executed against the index-returned tuple without using any
non-returnable columns.  (The restrictions imposed by check_index_only
guarantee this is possible, although we may have to recompute indexed
expressions.)  Support construction of that during setrefs.c
processing by marking IndexOnlyScan.indextlist entries as resjunk
if they can't be returned, rather than removing them entirely.
(We could alternatively require setrefs.c to look up the IndexOptInfo
again, but abusing resjunk this way seems like a reasonably safe way
to avoid needing to do that.)

This solution isn't great from an API-stability standpoint: if there
are any extensions out there that build IndexOnlyScan structs directly,
they'll be broken in the next minor releases.  However, only a very
invasive extension would be likely to do such a thing.  There's no
change in the Path representation, so typical planner extensions
shouldn't have a problem.

As before, back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: old_snapshot: add test for coverage
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a regression test for the contrib/old_snapshot extension so that its code coverage goes from 0% to 100%. It is a standalone test inside the extension.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers found that the test does not exercise the extension in a meaningful way. Daniel Gustafsson added that its LIMIT 0 could hide bugs behind a passing result. Tom Lane suggested testing old_snapshot through src/test/modules/snapshot_too_old instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looking at this I agree, this test doesn't provide enough to be of value and
the LIMIT 0 might even hide bugs under a postive test result.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert the commits related to allowing page lock to conflict among parallel group members.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert the commits related to allowing page lock to conflict among parallel group members.
Reverted commit(s): Allow page lock to conflict among parallel group members.; Add assert to ensure that page locks don't participate in deadlock cycle.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts the work done by commits 3ba59ccc89 and 72e78d831a.
Those commits were incorrect in asserting that we never acquire any other
heavy-weight lock after acquring page lock other than relation extension
lock. We can acquire a lock on catalogs while doing catalog look up after
acquring page lock.

This won't impact any existing feature but we need to think some other way
to achieve this before parallelizing other write operations or even
improving the parallelism in vacuum (like allowing multiple workers
for an index).

precedents_retrieved.title: Error "initial slot snapshot too large" in create replication slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes the "initial slot snapshot too large" error in CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT, which happens because SnapBuildInitialSnapshot puts top-level and subtransaction XIDs into the xip array and the count can exceed GetMaxSnapshotXidCount(). Versions tried excluding subtransactions, marking the snapshot takenDuringRecovery, asking the reorder buffer which XIDs are subtransactions, and finally using the subxip array as an extension of xip.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected to the last version because it adds a third way of using the xip and subxip arrays, and he saw no consensus on an approach. Earlier approaches failed for other reasons: the reorder buffer cannot reliably tell subtransactions apart, using takenDuringRecovery was rejected, and resizing xip made procarray.c and snapmgr.c too complicated. The author withdrew the entry for lack of a simple fix.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's bad enough that we
already use the xip/subxip arrays in two different ways depending on
the situation. Increasing that to three different ways seems painful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Continue to allow VACUUM to mark last block of index dirty even when there is no work to do.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Continue to allow VACUUM to mark last block of index dirty even when there is no work to do. Further analysis required. Revert of patch c1458cc495ff800cd176a1c2e56d8b62680d9b71
Reverted commit(s): Avoid marking buffer dirty when VACUUM has no work to do. When wal_level = 'hot_standby' we touched the last page of the relation during a VACUUM, even if nothing else had happened. That would alter the LSN of the last block and set the mtime of the relation file unnecessarily. Noted by Thom Brown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow "snapshot too old" error, to prevent bloat
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a GUC, old_snapshot_threshold, that lets vacuum remove tuples once a set number of transaction IDs has been consumed since a snapshot was taken. Each snapshot stores the insert LSN, and a scan that reads a heap or btree page with a newer LSN raises a "snapshot too old" error.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show the closing decision. Tom Lane objected to the feature itself, and both he and Andres Freund objected to an implementation that needs checks in the heap and in every index AM, which risks silently wrong query results. Andres Freund, Magnus Hagander and Simon Riggs found a threshold counted in transaction IDs hard to use, and Kevin Grittner began to discuss a time-based threshold instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Having to add checks to a large number of places is a recipe for silently wrong query results.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid duplicate XIDs at recovery when building initial snapshot - take 2
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch reverts commit 1df21ddb, which dropped duplicate XIDs from XLOG_RUNNING_XACTS records only when a standby applies them. Instead, GetRunningTransactionData() sorts the XIDs and subxids and removes duplicates on the primary whenever it finds a dummy two-phase proc entry, so the WAL record never holds duplicates.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Simon Riggs voted against the patch because it removes duplicates while holding ProcArrayLock, which is already a bottleneck, and he asked for proof that the performance cost is negligible. He also judged the committed fix in 1df21ddb sufficient and said the new patch was too complex to backpatch. The author agreed with these concerns and marked the patch returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I hadn't realised this patch holds ProcArrayLock while removing duplicates.
Now I know I vote against applying this patch unless someone can show that
the performance effects of doing so are negligable, which I doubt.

precedents_retrieved.title: Time-delayed logical replication subscriber
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Masahiko Sawada, Nathan Bossart, Amit Kapila
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a subscription option that delays applying logical replication changes by a set time, like recovery_min_apply_delay for standbys. Later versions moved the wait to the publisher as min_send_delay, with the walsender holding back each transaction and the combination with streaming = parallel disallowed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The subscriber confirms the flush LSN only after it commits the delayed transaction, so the publisher cannot advance restart_lsn or xmin during the delay. With delays of hours or days, WAL builds up on the publisher and VACUUM cannot remove dead rows, and users have no setting to avoid this. Reviewers asked for a different design, such as having the subscriber write decoded changes to disk first or adding a walreceiver process, and the author closed the entry to work on that.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IMO the current set of
trade-offs (e.g., unavoidable bloat and WAL buildup) would make this
feature virtually unusable for a lot of workloads, so it's probably worth
exploring an alternative approach.

precedents_retrieved.title: Apply worker fails if a relation is missing on subscriber even if refresh publication has not been refreshed yet
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch would let the logical replication apply worker skip changes for tables that were added to a publication but are not yet in pg_subscription_rel on the subscriber, because ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION has not been run. It would log a warning instead of failing repeatedly when such a table is missing on the subscriber.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila questioned whether the current ERROR behavior should be changed when no specific use case had been given. He noted that users can avoid the failure loop with the disable_on_error subscription parameter, and that silently skipping changes could surprise users whose subscriber-side setup is incomplete. The author said he had no specific use case, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I see your point but not sure if it is worth changing the
current behavior without any specific use case which we want to
address with this change.

precedents_retrieved.title: Iterating on IndexTuple attributes and nbtree page-level dynamic prefix truncation
precedents_retrieved.summary: Patch 0001 adds an API to iterate over index tuple attributes and reuse the offset of the last extracted attribute, so extracting all attributes costs O(n) instead of O(n*n) when attcacheoff cannot be used. Patch 0002 uses this to truncate attribute prefixes dynamically during nbtree binary search within a page, as a first step toward prefix truncation in nbtree.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author's own June 2021 benchmarks showed regressions in multi-column indexes that can use attcacheoff: about 2% for insert and 15% for reindex with both patches. The author said this had to be fixed before commit, but no fixed version appears in the thread. In December 2021 Daniel Gustafsson moved the entry forward and noted that the patch no longer applied and needed a rebase. The visible messages do not show a rebased version or the final decision.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Evidently, this needs improvements in the (likely common) attcacheoff-enabled multi-column case; as I don't think we can reasonably commit a 10+% regression.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
Reverted commit(s): Add regression test for bug fixed by recent refactoring.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
A view defined as "select <something> where false" had the curious property
that the system wouldn't check whether users had the privileges necessary
to select from it.  More generally, permissions checks could be skipped
for tables referenced in sub-selects or views that were proven empty by
constraint exclusion (although some quick testing suggests this seldom
happens in cases of practical interest).  This happened because the planner
failed to include rangetable entries for such tables in the finished plan.

This was noticed in connection with erroneous handling of materialized
views, but actually the issue is quite unrelated to matviews.  Therefore,
revert commit 200ba1667b3a8d7a9d559d2f05f83d209c9d8267 in favor of a more
direct test for the real problem.

Back-patch to 9.2 where the bug was introduced (by commit
7741dd6590073719688891898e85f0cb73453159).

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the corpus returned no earlier attempt at this idea. The only earlier designs are inside this thread: v1 to v4 (dropped by the author in message #18) and v5 to v10 (judged too expensive in message #33), and the current MVCC rescan does not repeat either of them.
From the standards and compatibility angle, the only issue is the behaviour change in the in-flight INSERT case for a stable-branch target. No new syntax, GUC, catalog or pg_dump surface is involved.
The current design does not change on-disk format, WAL, catalogs, wire protocol or extension ABI. The nbtree VACUUM bookkeeping invariant does not apply, because v11 and later do not touch nbtree.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes which snapshot the apply worker uses to find a row, adds no new privilege, role, setting or user-callable interface, and changes nothing about what a session can see or do. A local session that could hold an open INSERT to make the apply worker skip a publisher UPDATE already has INSERT privilege on that table and can change the row directly. Master's wait on an open local INSERT already lets such a session stall the apply worker, and v20 removes that wait, so this patch adds no new denial-of-service path. The new injection points exist only in builds made with --enable-injection-points. The visible material does not include the v20 code or thread.

The nbtree VACUUM bookkeeping invariant does not apply, because the current design does not change VACUUM. No committer who knows nbtree has engaged in the visible thread. That affects committability, not the verdict.

This is a correctness fix inside RelationFindReplTupleByIndex, and no existing feature, setting, contrib module or extension avoids the missed-tuple race in the apply worker. The fix reuses GetLatestSnapshot and table_tuple_lock, which the lookup already calls, so it adds no second mechanism. Documenting the race, as suggested in message #34, would describe the bug without fixing it.

This is a correctness fix, and two other people reproduced the lost update in logical replication (message #13, message #44). A demand objection does not fit. The open questions are design trade-offs, such as the in-flight INSERT case and back-patching, and other angles cover those.
